questions.question: Substances that can flow from one place to another are called:
questions.explanation:
Fluids are substances (liquids and gases) that do not have a fixed shape and flow under external
force.

questions.question: Fluid mechanics deals with the study of:
questions.explanation:
Fluid mechanics is divided into:
•
•

Fluid statics (fluids at rest)
Fluid dynamics (fluids in motion)

questions.question: The SI unit of pressure is:
questions.explanation: The SI unit of pressure is Pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

questions.question: One Pascal is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: Pressure = Force / Area → 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

questions.question: The upward force exerted by a fluid on an object immersed in it is called:
questions.explanation: Buoyancy (upthrust) is the upward force due to pressure difference in a fluid.

questions.question: According to Archimedes’ Principle, upthrust is equal to:
questions.explanation: Archimedes’ Principle: Upthrust = weight of displaced fluid.

questions.question: An object will float if its density is:

options.B: Less than or equal to the fluid

questions.explanation: An object floats if its density is less than or equal to the fluid.

questions.question: A ship floats on water because:

options.B: Its average density is less than water
options.D: It has no weight in sea

questions.explanation: Ships float because their average density is less than water due to hollow structure.

questions.question: The internal friction between different layers of a flowing fluid is called:
questions.explanation: Viscosity is internal friction between layers of a fluid.

questions.question: The SI unit of coefficient of viscosity is:
questions.explanation:
Unit of viscosity can be written as:
•
•
•

N s/m²
Pa·s
kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹


All are equivalent.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest viscosity?
questions.explanation: Honey has the highest viscosity among common fluids listed.

questions.question: Viscosity of liquids increases with temperature.
questions.explanation: In liquids, viscosity decreases as temperature increases.

questions.question: Viscosity of gases with increase in temperature:
questions.explanation: In gases, viscosity increases with temperature due to increased molecular motion.

questions.question: Stoke’s Law is applicable to:
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law applies to small spherical objects moving slowly in a fluid.

questions.question: Stoke’s Law is:
questions.explanation: Stokes’ Law: F = 6πηrv

questions.question: Maximum constant velocity of a falling body in fluid is:
questions.explanation: Terminal velocity is the constant maximum speed when net force becomes zero.

questions.question: Terminal velocity is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Terminal velocity is proportional to r².

questions.question: If radius is doubled, terminal velocity becomes:
questions.explanation: If radius doubles, terminal velocity becomes four times (proportional to r²).

questions.question: Streamline flow means:
questions.explanation: Streamline (laminar) flow: particles follow smooth, parallel paths.

questions.question: Irregular flow is called:
questions.explanation: Turbulent flow is irregular and chaotic.

questions.question: An ideal fluid is:
questions.explanation:
Ideal fluid is:
•
•
•

Non-viscous
Incompressible
Steady (streamline) flow

questions.question: Av is called:
questions.explanation: Av represents volume flow rate (discharge).

questions.question: Equation of continuity is based on:
questions.explanation: Continuity equation is based on conservation of mass.

questions.question: When area decreases, fluid speed:
questions.explanation: If area decreases, velocity increases (Av = constant).

questions.question: Bernoulli’s equation is based on:
questions.explanation: Bernoulli’s equation is based on conservation of energy.

questions.question: High speed fluid has:
questions.explanation: Higher velocity → lower pressure.

questions.question: Bernoulli equation is:
questions.explanation:
Bernoulli equation:
P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant

questions.question: Speed of efflux is given by:
questions.explanation: Speed of efflux is given by Torricelli’s theorem.

questions.question: Device to measure flow speed:
questions.explanation: Venturimeter is used to measure flow speed.

questions.question: Venturi effect describes:
questions.explanation: Venturi effect: pressure decreases when fluid speeds up in a constriction.

questions.question: Swing of cricket ball is due to:
questions.explanation: Swing of cricket ball is due to Bernoulli’s principle.

questions.question: Magnus effect relates to:
questions.explanation: Magnus effect acts on spinning objects in fluids.

questions.question: Atomizer works on:
questions.explanation: Atomizer works due to Bernoulli’s principle.

questions.question: Blood is:
questions.explanation: Blood is viscous due to cells and proteins.

questions.question: High blood pressure is due to:
questions.explanation: High blood pressure occurs due to narrowing of arteries.

questions.question: Zero viscosity state is:
questions.explanation: Superfluid has zero viscosity.

questions.question: Superfluids can:
questions.explanation:
Superfluids show:


•
•
•

No resistance
Wall climbing
Continuous flow

questions.question: Lift of airplane wing is due to:
questions.explanation: Lift is due to higher air speed above wing → lower pressure.

questions.question: Fog stays suspended due to:
questions.explanation: Fog stays suspended due to very low terminal velocity

questions.question: Dimensions of viscosity are:
questions.explanation:
The dimensions of coefficient of viscosity are [M L⁻¹ T⁻¹] (kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹), representing internal
resistance to flow.

questions.question: Bernoulli (horizontal pipe) reduces to:
questions.explanation:
For horizontal flow, height is constant, so Bernoulli’s equation reduces to:
P + ½ρv² = constant

questions.question: Unit of flow rate is:
questions.explanation: Flow rate = Area × Velocity = m² × m/s = m³/s.

questions.question: Fast heartbeat causes flow to be:
questions.explanation: High speed blood flow may become chaotic, leading to turbulence.

questions.question: Clouds stay due to:
questions.explanation: Cloud droplets remain suspended due to air resistance and viscous drag.

questions.question: To increase water speed from pipe:
questions.explanation: Reducing pipe area increases fluid velocity (continuity equation: Av = constant).

questions.question: Turbulent flow example:
questions.explanation: Smoke forming irregular swirls is a classic example of turbulent flow.

questions.question: Viscosity is due to:
questions.explanation:
Viscosity arises from:
•
•

Cohesive forces in liquids
Molecular collisions in gases

questions.question: If velocity doubles, drag becomes:
questions.explanation: Stokes’ drag is directly proportional to velocity, so doubling velocity doubles force.

questions.question: Terminal velocity occurs when:
questions.explanation:
Terminal velocity occurs when:
Weight = Buoyant force + Drag force

questions.question: Density of water is:
questions.explanation:
Water density is:
•
•

1000 kg/m³
1 g/cm³
Both are equivalent.

questions.question: Relative density has units:
questions.explanation: Relative density is a ratio of densities, so it has no unit.

questions.question: Hydrometer measures:
questions.explanation: A hydrometer measures relative density of liquids.

questions.question: Superfluid flows with:
questions.explanation: Superfluid flows with zero resistance due to quantum effects.

questions.question: Bernoulli not applicable to:
questions.explanation: Bernoulli’s equation does not apply to turbulent flow because energy is not conserved smoothly.

questions.question: Net force at terminal velocity:
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, net force = 0 (no acceleration).

questions.question: Torricelli is based on:
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s theorem is derived from Bernoulli’s equation.

questions.question: Pressure at lake bottom depends on:
questions.explanation:
Pressure in a fluid depends on:
•
•
•

Depth
Density
Gravity
P = ρgh

questions.question: Venturi minimum pressure at:
questions.explanation: At the narrow section of a Venturi tube, velocity is maximum and pressure is minimum.

questions.question: Ping-pong balls in airflow:
questions.explanation: Air between ping-pong balls moves faster → lower pressure → balls move closer.

questions.question: SI unit of flow rate:
questions.explanation: Flow rate unit is m³/s (volume per second).

questions.question: Barometer measures:
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: Upthrust depends on:
questions.explanation: Upthrust depends on the volume of fluid displaced.

questions.question: Wood floats with half submerged density:
questions.explanation:
If half volume is submerged:
ρobject = ½ ρwater = 500 kg/m³.

questions.question: Continuity ratio v1/v2 equals:
questions.explanation:
From continuity equation:
v1/v2 = A2/A1 = (r2/r1)²

questions.question: Steady flow means velocity:
questions.explanation: Steady flow means velocity at a point does not change with time.

questions.question: Streamline tangent shows:
questions.explanation: A streamline’s tangent gives the direction of velocity.

questions.question: Streamlines cannot:
questions.explanation: Streamlines cannot intersect, as that would give two velocities at one point.

questions.question: Terminal velocity is inversely proportional to:
questions.explanation: Terminal velocity is inversely proportional to viscosity.

questions.question: Incompressible fluid means constant:
questions.explanation: Incompressible fluid means density remains constant.

questions.question: Blood incompressible means:
questions.explanation: Blood is nearly incompressible; its volume does not change significantly under pressure.

questions.question: Air speed above umbrella causes:
questions.explanation: Faster air above umbrella → lower pressure → lift upward.

questions.question: Venturi meter works on:
questions.explanation: Venturi meter works on pressure-velocity relationship (Bernoulli principle).

questions.question: Torricelli speed depends on:
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s speed depends only on height of liquid column (h).

questions.question: Spinning ball curves due to:
questions.explanation: Spinning ball curves due to pressure difference (Magnus effect).

questions.question: Non-viscous fluid means:
questions.explanation: Non-viscous fluid has zero internal friction.

questions.question: Reynolds number tells:
questions.explanation: Reynolds number determines whether flow is laminar or turbulent.

questions.question: Laminar flow Reynolds number is:
questions.explanation: Low Reynolds number indicates laminar flow.

questions.question: Carburetor works on:
questions.explanation: Carburetors work using the Venturi effect (pressure drop increases fuel mixing).

questions.question: Viscosity in liquids is due to:
questions.explanation: Viscosity in liquids is mainly due to cohesive intermolecular forces.

questions.question: Viscosity in gases is due to:
questions.explanation: In gases, viscosity is due to momentum transfer between molecules.

questions.question: Upthrust formula is:
questions.explanation: Loss in weight = upthrust = W − W’.

questions.question: Helium balloon rises because:
questions.explanation: Helium balloon rises because its density is lower than air.

questions.question: Fluid pressure acts:
questions.explanation: Fluid pressure acts equally in all directions (Pascal’s law).

questions.question: Bernoulli effect used in:
questions.explanation:
Bernoulli effect is used in:
•
•
•

Chimneys
Blood flow
Sailing
All of these.

questions.question: Terminal velocity depends on:
questions.explanation: Terminal velocity increases with density difference (ρ − σ).

questions.question: Vertical pipe Bernoulli includes:
questions.explanation: In vertical pipes, potential energy term ρgh must be included.

questions.question: Flow rate unit equals:
questions.explanation: Flow rate = area × velocity = m³/s.

questions.question: Superfluidity first seen in:
questions.explanation: Superfluidity was first observed in liquid helium (Helium-4).
